topic: The Geometry of Cramer's Rule: Solving with Areas
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

outline.topic: The Geometry of Cramer's Rule: Solving with Areas
outline.target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Quest of the Delivery Drone
sections.content: Introduce a scenario where a delivery drone must reach a target point 'b' using two thrusters that move in fixed directions (vectors v1 and v2). The goal is to find exactly how much power (x and y) to give to each thruster. This sets up the system of linear equations Ax = b.
sections.example: A drone needs to reach coordinates (7, 6). Thruster 1 moves it along [2, 1] and Thruster 2 moves it along [1, 2]. We need to solve x[2, 1] + y[1, 2] = [7, 6].

sections.title: Prerequisite: Determinant as Area
sections.content: Briefly recap that the determinant of a 2x2 matrix represents the 'signed area' of the parallelogram formed by its column vectors. Visualize two vectors v1 and v2 forming a colored parallelogram in the Cartesian plane.
sections.example: Show a matrix with columns [2, 1] and [1, 2]. Animate the parallelogram they form and highlight its area (3 units squared) as the 'Base Area'.

sections.title: The Geometric Transformation
sections.content: Explain that the target vector 'b' is a linear combination of the basis vectors. Visually demonstrate that scaling v1 by 'x' and v2 by 'y' creates a new parallelogram whose diagonal is 'b'.
sections.example: Show the vector v1 being stretched by 'x' and v2 by 'y' so that their sum perfectly lands on the drone's target.

sections.title: The 'Shifted Parallelogram' Trick
sections.content: Introduce the key geometric insight: If we replace the first vector (v1) with the target vector (b), the area of the resulting parallelogram is exactly 'x' times the original area. This is because the 'height' relative to v2 is scaled by 'x' while v2 remains the same.
sections.example: Animate a transition where v1 is swapped out for 'b'. Show that the area of the parallelogram formed by (b, v2) is significantly larger than the original (v1, v2) parallelogram.

sections.title: Deriving the Ratio
sections.content: Show the math through the visual: x = Area(b, v2) / Area(v1, v2). Explain that since the determinant is the area, x is simply the determinant of the modified matrix divided by the determinant of the original matrix A.
sections.example: Calculate Det(b, v2) = 8 and Det(v1, v2) = 3. Therefore, the power for Thruster 1 (x) is 8/3. Repeat visually for y by swapping v2 with 'b'.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize that Cramer's rule isn't just a dry formula, but a ratio of areas (or volumes in 3D). It measures how much the 'output' vector contributes to the space compared to the original basis vectors.
sections.example: A final visual summary showing the drone reaching the target, overlaying the two 'Area Ratios' next to the final x and y coordinates.

storyboard.title: The Quest of the Delivery Drone
lecture_lines: A drone needs to reach target point b.
Two thrusters move in fixed directions, v1 and v2.
We must find the power x and y required.
animations: Fade in a drone icon at the origin and a target marker at (7, 6).
Draw vector v1=[2,1] in #00FF00 and vector v2=[1,2] in #0000FF from the origin.
Display the equation x[2, 1] + y[1, 2] = [7, 6] in #FFFFFF at the top.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: The determinant represents the area of a parallelogram.
Columns v1 and v2 define the base area.
This area is the determinant of matrix A.
animations: Draw vectors v1=[2,1] and v2=[1,2] starting from the origin.
Animate the construction of a parallelogram using v1 and v2, filled with #FFFF00 at 0.3 opacity.
Display the label 'Area = Det(A) = 3' in #FFFF00 next to the parallelogram.

storyboard.title: The Geometric Transformation
lecture_lines: Target b is a sum of scaled vectors.
We scale v1 by x and v2 by y.
Their sum reaches the drone's destination exactly.
animations: Show v1 and v2 being scaled by factors x and y as dashed lines.
Animate the vector addition of scaled v1 and scaled v2 to reach the target b=[7, 6].
Highlight the resulting diagonal vector b in #FF0000.

storyboard.title: The 'Shifted Parallelogram' Trick
lecture_lines: Let's replace the first vector v1 with b.
This creates a new, shifted parallelogram.
Its height remains relative to vector v2.
The new area is scaled exactly by x.
This is the key insight of Cramer's rule.
animations: Highlight the original yellow parallelogram formed by vectors v1 and v2.
Smoothly morph vector v1 into the target vector b=[7, 6] in #FF0000.
Construct a new parallelogram using b and v2, colored in #FFA500.
Flash the orange area to emphasize it is 'x' times the original yellow area.
Display 'Area(b, v2) = x * Area(v1, v2)' in #FFFFFF at the bottom.

storyboard.title: Deriving the Ratio
lecture_lines: We calculate x as a ratio of areas.
x equals the new area divided by original.
This is the determinant ratio of modified matrices.
Similarly, find y by swapping v2 with b.
Cramer's rule solves variables using determinants.
animations: Display the formula 'x = Det(b, v2) / Det(v1, v2)' in #FFFFFF.
Animate the calculation showing Det(b, v2) = 8 and Det(A) = 3, yielding x = 8/3.
Swap the visualization to show a parallelogram formed by v1 and b in #00FFFF.
Display the formula 'y = Det(v1, b) / Det(v1, v2)' and show y = 5/3.
Highlight the final coordinate pair (8/3, 5/3) in #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Summary and Intuition
lecture_lines: Cramer's rule is a geometric ratio of areas.
It measures how b contributes to the space.
The formula works for any number of dimensions.
Our delivery drone has found its precise path.
Linear algebra solves problems with geometry.
animations: Show the drone moving to (7, 6) using thruster powers 8/3 and 5/3.
Display the text 'Cramer\'s Rule: A Ratio of Areas' in #FFFFFF.
Fade out vectors and parallelograms, leaving only the summary text on screen.
